title: DarwinGame: Playing Tournaments for Tuning Applications in Noisy Cloud Environments
problem: Existing application performance tuners (OpenTuner, ActiveHarmony, BLISS) implicitly assume a dedicated interference-free execution environment; when used as-is in shared cloud environments with unpredictable co-tenant interference, they produce suboptimal tuning configurations that are more than 40% away from optimal because interference levels differ across configuration evaluations, causing the tuner to misrank configurations.
motivation: Application developers increasingly tune on shared cloud infrastructure (due to cost, device availability, and deployment-environment fidelity), but uncontrollable background interference invalidates the relative performance measurements that all existing tuners rely upon.
method: DarwinGame runs multiple copies of an application with different configurations on the same virtual machine simultaneously, so they all face the same interference—this lets you directly compare them rather than guessing their performance from separate runs with different interference levels. It searches 10,000 configurations through four tournament stages: (1) a Swiss-style regional phase where the search space divides into 10,000 regions and configurations compete in parallel with early stopping when a winner emerges (judged by how much work gets done), (2) a double-elimination phase where both winners and losers advance to re-compete (judged on speed and consistency), (3) a barrage-style playoff where top survivors compete head-to-head without early stopping, and (4) a final match. This finds configurations that are both fast and reliable under cloud interference.
key_novelty: The core innovation is running multiple application copies with different configurations on the same virtual machine so they experience identical interference, enabling direct comparison, then using a tournament structure (Swiss regional, double-elimination global, barrage playoff, finals) to find configurations that are both fast and reliable under unpredictable cloud interference.
contributions: Introduction of interference-aware cloud performance tuning as a new research area and first solution (DarwinGame).
Tournament-based design with Swiss, double-elimination, and barrage phases that systematically identify configurations with low execution time and low interference sensitivity.
Integration mechanism allowing DarwinGame to enhance existing tuners (OpenTuner, BLISS) as a subspace search oracle.

Evaluation on AWS (m5.8xlarge, 32 vCPUs) with Redis, GROMACS, FFmpeg, LAMMPS: >27% execution time reduction over existing tuners, <0.5% performance variability, >15% improvement when integrated with existing tuners.

metrics.speedup: >27% reduction in execution time vs. OpenTuner/BLISS/ActiveHarmony in cloud environments
metrics.accuracy: 4.2% above optimal on average (vs. 40%+ for next best tuner BLISS)
metrics.other: <0.5% performance variability; >15% improvement when integrated with existing tuners

limitations: DarwinGame targets static tunable parameters only and does not provide provable theoretical bounds on convergence due to the unpredictable nature of cloud interference; co-location within a VM introduces additional noise that can affect smaller configurations.
primary_theme: tournament-based application tuning robust to cloud interference
